transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2027-05-06 14:30 UTC
- Duration: 48 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jonah Reed (Redwood SE), Dr. Elena Voss (Argo CTO), Markus Klein (Argo Head of Infra), Sana Iqbal (Argo Procurement)

Summary:
High-level: Argo wants to top-up their retainer and run a small EU on-prem pilot to validate latency and data residency for regulatory pipelines. Agreed to run dedicated throughput tests and to exchange an amendment to extend the contract term with committed capacity. Discussed tradeoffs between hosted fallback vs full private deployment, SOC2 and KMS needs plus pilot success criteria.

Topics covered:
- Retainer top-up mechanics and term extension
- EU on-prem pilot scope and constraints (data residency, network/firewall requirements)
- Dedicated capacity sizing and latency targets
- Security controls: SSO, KMS, audit logs, SOC2 evidence
- Next steps and owners

Transcript body:
[00:00:00] Maya: alright folks we can get started, thanks for joining, i know we have a pretty packed agenda today to go over the retainer top up and the eu on prem pilot
[00:00:15] Elena: yep thanks maya, we wanted a tight sync — main ask is: can we get predictable latency for our clinical inference pipelines while keeping data inside eu, and also figure out committed pricing for the next 12 months as usage is spiky
[00:00:36] Jonah: cool, quick ask from our side, do you expect most inference to be batch (scheduled) or real time? that changes the dedicated sizing and the cache strategy
[00:00:45] Markus: it's a mix: 70% batch overnight but the 30% realtime matters — the clinician dashboard needs sub-300ms tail latency for short prompts (~256 tokens)
[00:01:05] Speaker 3: (mumble) sub 300? 
[00:01:07] Jonah: got it, sub-300ms for 256 tokens is doable with a dedicated pool if we tune batching and keep kv warm; we'll demo the difference in the benchmark runs
[00:01:25] Maya: on the contract side, you're looking at top-up retainer vs a full capacity shift, are you thinking a 6 month or 12 month commitment?
[00:01:35] Sana: procurement here, short term we prefer 6 months but if pricing looks favorable we can do 12. we need clear break clauses and an SLA for throughput/latency in the amendment
[00:01:50] Jonah: we can propose tiers for 6/12/24 months — pricing delta comes from committed units and reserved GPU pool sizes; dedicated vs hosted fallback paths affect cost too because hosted bursting is charged differently
[00:02:07] Elena: also we need to lock down security — SOC 2 evidence, SSO via SAML/Okta, KMS integration for key control, and audit logs accessible for our compliance team
[00:02:24] Maya: yes we'll attach our SOC2 report and a KMS integration guide, okta SAML is supported, and we can surface audit logs in the console. for on-prem we provide a private control plane option plus an on-prem runtime package but of course that requires network setup and an NDA
[00:02:42] Markus: about the on-prem pilot, this is where some of the nuance is — we want to keep data on-prem, but still use Redwood's control plane for rollouts if possible. are there examples of customers doing hybrid control plane?
[00:02:55] Jonah: yeah a number of customers run the private control plane in their VPC; the runtime talks back to control plane endpoints over a tunnel — we can show the network diagram. caveat: metrics and tracing sometimes need explicit allow-lists and we redacted a few hostnames in earlier docs, transcription sorry — (laughs)
[00:03:18] Elena: haha noted. what's the expected lead time for standing up a 4-GPU dedicated pool in eu-west?
[00:03:25] Maya: provisioning to reserved is typically 2–4 weeks depending on capacity in the region; a pilot using your on-prem appliances could be shorter if infra is ready — depends on firewall rules and cert provisioning
[00:03:40] Markus: our security team also asked about HSM/KMS for key custody. we can't have keys stored in a multi-tenant vault for certain datasets
[00:03:49] Jonah: we support customer-managed keys via KMS and HSM integrations for private deployments; for hosted we can do envelope encryption with customer KMS in some cloud providers — but for the strictest control you want the private on-prem runtime and customer KMS/HSM
[00:04:05] Sana: procurement note — we need a pricing worksheet that shows base retainer, committed units, and unit price for bursting vs hosted fallbacks; also cancellation terms
[00:04:18] Maya: understood, i'll prepare an amendment + pricing scenarios. also we discussed pilot success criteria — maybe we should codify them now?
[00:04:29] Elena: success = 1) median latency under 120ms for 64-token inferences, 2) 95th percentile under 300ms for 256 tokens, 3) no exfiltration risk and KMS in place, 4) ability to route degraded traffic to hosted fallback under cost/time thresholds
[00:04:49] Jonah: that's a good set; for the latency numbers we'll need to run both cold-cache and warmed-cache scenarios, and include continuous batching behavior; i'll include quantized model runs since you plan to use smaller variants in prod
[00:05:05] Speaker 2: (crosstalk) quick question about models — are you planning to use open weights or an enterprise model?
[00:05:12] Elena: we'll use an open foundation model fine-tuned in-house; need to validate quantized 4-bit performance for cost reasons
[00:05:20] Jonah: okay good, quantization will help; one callout about accuracy degradation — we'll run a prompt set you provide and create a small eval harness so we can measure regressions between full-precision and quantized runs
[00:05:34] Maya: on the fallback story, we recommend a policy: primary private runtime, fallback to Redwood-hosted identical model family with traffic shaping after X% queue or Yms latency — that reduces downtime risk but does increase egress/hosting costs
[00:05:52] Markus: what's the uplift on cost if we keep hosted fallback enabled? ballpark?
[00:05:59] Jonah: ballpark depends on burst frequency; if you reserve a 4-GPU pool and use fallback for rare spikes (<5% traffic) uplift is ~15–25% on unit cost in our example worksheet; if you rely on hosted for 30% of traffic uplift becomes large ~2x cost on that portion
[00:06:21] Sana: that's helpful, procurement will need the worksheet to model those scenarios. also need an SLA addendum for 99.9% uptime and an escalation path
[00:06:31] Maya: we'll provide draft SLA text and escalation contacts.
[00:06:36] Elena: timeline — we want pilot to start in June, run 6 weeks, and then decide on committed top-up by mid July. is that feasible?
[00:06:45] Jonah: timeline feasible if we get on-prem readiness and NDA done in two weeks; benchmarks to be shared within one week after runs
[00:06:53] Maya: ok action owners: jonah runs benchmarks; maya sends amendment; elena to share compliance checklist and sample prompts.
[00:07:05] Speaker 1: (short silence)
[00:07:10] Jonah: small technical note — for the throughput test i'll run a 1k token and 256 token workload, measure p50/p95, cold starts, kv warm, and also run a quantized 4-bit model variant; i'll include config for batch size and max latency SLO
[00:07:26] Markus: for the network, we'll need a list of egress IP ranges and the control-plane FQDNs so our firewall team can whitelist them; can you share that?
[00:07:35] Maya: yes, i'll include a security checklist and the CIDR list; note some hostnames rotate per deployment but we'll give the canonical endpoints
[00:07:45] Sana: and pricing — can you include an example monthly amortized cost for the 6 month vs 12 month committed tiers? we want to justify a 12 month if it saves >20%
[00:07:56] Maya: yes, we'll model it.
[00:07:59] Elena: any blockers on Redwood side about the hybrid control-plane?
[00:08:05] Jonah: none technical, just network and cert provisioning; operationally we do need an SRE contact on your side for cert rotation and troubleshooting during pilot
[00:08:14] Markus: that we can pair on, i'll assign an engineer.
[00:08:18] Maya: great. do we want a follow-up demo of the control-plane UI and audit logs for your security team?
[00:08:24] Elena: yes, please. security wants to see audit log retention and role based access controls in the console
[00:08:32] Maya: ok i'll schedule a 30 minute deep dive with our CSM and product security next week — suggest May 11th at 15:00 UTC?
[00:08:41] Sana: that works for us.
[00:08:45] Jonah: last technical note: please include a small prompt set (10–20 prompts) that represent clinical vs admin traffic so our evals match production signals
[00:08:55] Elena: will do.
[00:09:00] Maya: thanks everyone — quick recap of next steps then we'll close: jonah to run and share benchmark spreadsheet; maya to send amendment and cidr/security checklist; elena to share prompts and compliance checklist; schedule control-plane demo with security on May 11th; target pilot start early June.
[00:09:20] Markus: good recap. thanks.
[00:09:24] Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up in CRM and slack.

End of transcript.
